## What it is

- The **Precision Bass** was first offered for sale in **October 1951** (Wikipedia, "Fender Precision Bass").
- Fender chose a **34-inch scale** "after much trial and error"; it became the standard for full-scale electric basses (Wikipedia).
- Its biggest change came in **1957**: a new **split-coil** pickup. It has stayed on Precision Basses ever since (Wikipedia).
- Four strings, tuned E A D G, an octave below a guitar's lowest four.

## Its sound

- The first Precision pickup was a single coil, and Leo Fender did not like its hum (Wikipedia).
- He split it into **two coils**, "wired out of phase with the magnets oriented with reverse polarities" (Wikipedia). Hum makes opposite voltages in the two halves and cancels; the strings' signal adds. It works like a humbucker.
- Each half sits under **two strings** (E-A in one half, D-G in the other), so the two halves are at slightly different places on the string (which half is nearer the bridge: this page reads photos, unverified).
- Two coils in series, a lot of wire: a low resonance, so a round, full, dark sound.
- One volume, one tone. The tone knob only cuts treble: it is passive, with no battery.

## The controls

The P-Bass's control area, drawn after the real one (positions approximate). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), then press a ▶ button. The sound is this site's physical model of a plucked bass string through these pickups and this wiring, into an amp; nobody has compared it with a real bass. The picture under the buttons shows the harmonics of the open A string (55 Hz) at the jack (bars) and the circuit alone (line).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="pbass" data-set="{}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Everything up.</b> The plain P sound: round and full.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="pbass" data-set="{&quot;tone&quot;:3}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Tone down to 3.</b> Darker, thumpier: an older soul and Motown kind of sound (a description, not a measured setting).</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="pbass" data-set="{&quot;tone&quot;:0}" data-play="pluck"><p><b>Tone at 0.</b> Very dark: almost only the low harmonics.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="pbass" data-set="{&quot;vol&quot;:6}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Volume at 6.</b> Quieter and a little duller: the pot's resistance and the cable take treble away.</p></div>
```
